# Motus — early ALS detection, from how you move

**BioHacks 2026.** ALS is usually caught late. The signal that something is
changing shows up in movement — how you speak, how you type, how you write —
months before a clinic visit scores it.

Motus measures those three channels at home, against **your own baseline**,
and shows the drift. Not "you look like an ALS patient" — "this is slower
than you were in August, and it has been for 66 sessions."

---

## Run it

```bash
npm install --prefix frontend && npm run dev --prefix frontend
```

Opens on <http://localhost:5173>. The dashboard at `/home` renders
immediately against deterministic sample data — no Supabase, no backend, no
keys needed. It shows a **"Sample data"** badge while that's the source.

Sign-in needs Supabase keys; copy `frontend/.env.example` to `frontend/.env`
and fill them in.

## What it shows

180 days of at-home sessions across three domains:

```
Speech       (bulbar)       rate · DDK · pause ratio · phonation · HNR
Typing       (fine motor)   speed · inter-key interval · hold · corrections
Handwriting  (fine motor)   stroke velocity · jerk · pressure · spiral
```

Each feature is z-scored against the person's own first 28 days. A domain
goes **Watch** at −1σ and **Flagged** at −2σ, and only when the change
persists — not on one bad day. The sample tells a bulbar-onset story: speech
drifts first, then typing, then handwriting.

Nothing here is a diagnosis, and every screen says so.

## Also in this repo

| | |
|---|---|
| `contract/` | Schema + validator for `data/pipeline.json` |
| `docs/` | Specs, research, decisions, status |

The drug-repurposing pipeline and FaceCheck have their own branches. See [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) for the map.

## Standalone diagnostic tests

Launch the complete session on this Mac:

```sh
cd ~/Documents/BioHacks && python3 master-app/diagnostic_complete.py
```

The master app opens at http://127.0.0.1:8772. Select **Begin** on each animated introduction, then complete the facial expression challenge, passage reading, and line tracing in order. Review each test’s results and select **Proceed To Next Test**. The speech test includes three passages with word-level playback. After all five tracing overlays, **Complete Diagnostic** opens the thank-you screen. Camera and microphone access are requested by the individual tests.

On a fresh checkout, run `bash facial-test/setup.sh` and `bash speech-test-good/setup.sh` first. The launcher reuses running local test servers or starts them as needed. Control-C stops the launcher and the servers it started.

| Directory | Contents |
|---|---|
| [speech-test-good](speech-test-good/) | Current transcript-only passage test and Mac launcher |
| [speech-tests-backup](speech-tests-backup/) | Earlier speech tests, calibrated comparison demo, and VOC-ALS experiments |
| [facial-test](facial-test/) | Four-round POSTER++ webcam expression challenge |
| [line-test](line-test/index.html) | Standalone mouse and trackpad tracing challenge |
| [SVD-diagnostic](SVD-diagnostic/) | EMG SVD analysis and speech SVD comparisons |

## Working here

**Read [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) first**, then
[`docs/STATUS.md`](docs/STATUS.md). Four people are working in parallel; those
two files are how we avoid building the same thing twice.

```bash
npm test --prefix contract     # before you push anything touching the contract
```
---
# Findings — what we learned the hard way

**Tasks are not here any more.** Work is claimed in GitHub Issues:

```bash
gh issue list                  # what's open
gh issue list --assignee ""    # what's free
gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me
```

This file is for the other thing: numbers that turned out wrong, two people
colliding, traps that cost someone an hour. Things you need *before* you
pitch or before you merge, which don't belong in a task.

Add to it when you find one. It's cheaper than the next person finding it
again.

Last updated: **2026-11-08**

---

## ⚠ Two people are building the same pipeline right now

**Jeremy** has the five-stage discovery pipeline in `frontend/` — scripted
TypeScript, `MATCHES` hand-written, labelled "Simulated".

**Levi** has `backend/query-generation/` on `agentic-query-generation` —
**five real Python agents** (`disease-indications`, `genes-targets`,
`pathways-processes`, `safety-interactions-class`, `symptoms-function`)
plus `ranking/intersection.py` and `ranking/fallback.py`, grounded in DRKG
and gated on human ALS exposure.

That is the same five agents, twice. One is the demo, one is the engine,
and **they share no git history** — `agentic-query-generation` has no merge
base with `main`.

Whoever picks this up: the cheapest win in the repo is making Jeremy's
`PipelineEvent` stream come from Levi's agents instead of a timer. The seam
already exists. Talk before either of you builds further.

**Neo** has a third piece, `agent/` (PR #4): a Claude orchestrator that plans
ALS criteria and runs parallel LLM sub-agents that return drug-free *target
profiles* (genes + desired action, pathways, site). These are the anchors
Levi's DRKG agents need, and its SSE stream is a live source for Jeremy's
`PipelineEvent`s. How to combine all three without building a fourth:
[`RESEARCH_AGENT_HANDOFF.md`](RESEARCH_AGENT_HANDOFF.md).

## Found while auditing — read before you pitch

Measured against Neo's real `pipeline.json` on `cursor/pipeline-graph-ui`,
not the sample. Full citations in [`FUS_RESEARCH.md`](FUS_RESEARCH.md).

1. **The graveyard overstates `never_arrived`.** 24 `never_arrived` / 8
   `arrived_failed` — but **21 of the 24 have no BBB prediction at all**
   (biologics, or out of the model's domain). `src/merge.py:211-214` files
   "no prediction" as `never_arrived`. Only ceftriaxone (p 0.39),
   pentoxifylline (0.29) and pioglitazone (0.29) are actually predicted
   BBB-negative. Honest split: **3 / 8 / 21 undetermined.** Say "3 predicted
   never-arrived, 21 we can't call" on stage, never "24" — a judge who knows
   gabapentin crosses the BBB will catch it.
2. **Same error in the funnel.** "2,440 eliminated: predicted BBB-negative"
   is **1,593 predicted negative + 847 out of domain.** The honest number is
   still the strong one: **1,593 approved drugs the model says can't cross.**
   That is the FUS-unlocked pool — use it.
3. **Discovery stage 3 is fake while a real one exists.** `MATCHES` in
   `frontend/src/lib/pipeline.ts` is hand-written; Neo's `src/drkg.py` loads
   the real DRKG TransE vectors. Note DRKG embeds *entities*, not text, so a
   profile has to become DRKG genes before it has a vector — Jeremy's
   profiles already list target genes, so that bridge is short.
4. **Three knowledge graphs and two FaceChecks exist.** Graph: Neo's
   `GraphCanvas`, Henri's stale `KnowledgeGraph.tsx`, and a "coming soon"
   placeholder on `main`. FaceCheck: Neo's TS original and Levi's JS port.
   Pick one of each.

## If main gives you a `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo` conflict — read this first

**Jeremy, this is the one you're hitting.** `frontend/tsconfig.tsbuildinfo`
is TypeScript's incremental build cache. It was committed by mistake, it
rewrites itself on every single build, so it conflicted constantly. `main`
untracked it on 2026-11-07 and it's gitignored now.

content.text:
I moved everything into `frontend/` and `backend/`. It's all staged on `repo-cleaning`. I haven't committed.

```
frontend/              (unchanged)
backend/
  agent/               ← was agent/
  contract/            ← was contract/
  data/                ← was data/
  diagnostics/         ← master-app, facial-test, line-test, speech-test-good,
                          speech-tests-backup, SVD-diagnostic
  query-generation/    (unchanged)
  validation/          (unchanged)
docs/  README.md  AGENTS.md  CLAUDE.md
```

**No code changed.** The 86 moves are plain renames, and every moved module finds its files relative to its own folder, so nothing broke:
- `agent/config.py` now looks for its data in `backend/data/`, which is where `data/` went. I checked that `backend/data/pipeline.json`, `backend/data/patient/` and your `backend/agent/.env` are all found. I moved whole folders rather than individual tracked files, so ignored local files like that `.env` came along.
- The six diagnostic folders sit next to each other again, so the launcher's references to the facial, speech and line tests still resolve. So do the SVD scripts' references to `speech-tests-backup`.
- Contract tests pass (9/9). The sample `pipeline.json` still validates.

I did not start the Python servers or run the agent's own tests; I only checked that their file paths resolve.

**Three ways you run things have changed:**
- Contract commands are now `npm test --prefix backend/contract`.
- The research agent now runs from inside `backend/`, e.g. `cd backend && python -m agent.api`.
- The diagnostic launcher is now `python3 backend/diagnostics/master-app/diagnostic_complete.py`.

**Docs updated to match:** `AGENTS.md` (directory table and commands), `README.md`, `.gitignore`, `docs/CONTRACT.md` (which also had a stale `--prefix app` command), and the FaceCheck and Discovery specs. The two research-agent docs and `backend/agent/README.md` have a lot of `agent/…` paths and commands, so instead of rewriting each one I added a note at the top saying those paths are relative to `backend/`. I logged the change in `docs/DECISIONS.md` and added a note for teammates to `docs/STATUS.md`.

**Things to know:**
- **I couldn't claim a GitHub issue.** `gh` isn't installed in this shell, so this move isn't recorded in the issue list. It touches a lot of shared paths, so tell the team.
- **Other open branches will mostly merge cleanly.** Git follows the renames. The catch is that any *new* file someone added under an old top-level path (e.g. `data/…` on `cursor/pipeline-graph-ui`) will reappear at the old location after merging, and will need to be moved under `backend/` by hand.

content.text:
Only one file in it is tracked, `.workspace/README.md`, and that's deliberate. Anything else you put in `.workspace/` stays local.

The rule is in `.gitignore`:

```gitignore
.workspace/*
!.workspace/README.md
```

The first line ignores everything inside the folder, and the second makes an exception for the README. The README explains what the folder is for: your personal `CLAUDE.md`, scratch scripts, notes and test `.env` files that shouldn't end up in the team's diffs. It's tracked so the folder exists, with that explanation, for anyone who clones the repo. It was added in commit `4992733` ("Move the task board to GitHub Issues").

The pattern is `.workspace/*` instead of `.workspace/` for a reason: if git ignores the whole directory, it never looks inside it, so the exception for the README would never apply.

If you'd rather the folder not be tracked at all, I can delete the README with `git rm` and change the rule to plain `.workspace/`. The cost is that new clones won't get the folder or the note explaining it.
